analysis: Examined the two base-side excerpts of fixtures/prompt-contract/v1/production_vectors.json (lines 43523-44942). They contain only public synthetic test vectors: tool-call messages, json_object and json_schema response_format cases, template_input rendering, prompt_contract_id values, block_boundaries chain hashes and token_ids. They hold no secrets, keys, attestation data, authorization state or real consumer content; the prompt text is 'Public synthetic cache-parity input'. The patch metadata shows head-side edits: an added additional_context {enable_thinking:false}, changed token counts and chain hashes, and removed or shifted token_ids. These are fixture-only changes with no runtime code, authorization or network surface in the supplied evidence. They touch the prefix-cache/prompt-contract area (T-041 / TB-007), but the only effect is test-vector expectations for prompt rendering and cache block hashing. The head-side text and the consuming code (prompt contract hashing, cache keying, scope_id handling) were not supplied, and the patch excerpt is truncated. I therefore cannot verify that the updated chain hashes and contract ID match the implementation, or that the added additional_context is excluded from, or correctly bound into, cache keys. A mismatch would be a correctness or cache-parity issue rather than a demonstrated security regression. The unchanged prompt_contract_id on some vectors versus the changed template_input is worth a check by integration. No TB-011, TB-002 or A-016 authorization behavior is changed. No findings.
